title: Inertia and balanced forces
target: Predict motion when the net force is zero.
criteria: Add forces to decide whether they balance.
Predict constant velocity when net force is zero.
Explain why changing direction requires net force.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A cart has 14 N right and 14 N left horizontally. What is horizontal net force?
cpa.guide: Equal opposing forces sum to zero.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: An object has 18 N up, 18 N down, and 5 N right with no left force. Are all forces balanced?
options: No; net force is 41 N down.
No; the net force is 5 N right.
Yes; the vertical forces cancel everything.
Yes; any equal pair means full equilibrium.
cpa.guide: Balance must be checked on each axis.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A puck moves west on an ideal frictionless horizontal surface after the push ends. What happens to its horizontal velocity?
options: It steadily decreases without a force.
cpa.guide: Zero horizontal net force means constant horizontal velocity.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A drifting probe has zero net force for 20 s. Which motion is possible?
options: Straight motion at a constant nonzero velocity.
cpa.guide: Newton’s first law allows rest or uniform straight motion.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Why does turning at constant speed require a net force?
options: It does not require a force.
cpa.guide: A changing velocity requires acceleration and therefore net force.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A claim says zero net force means the object is stationary. Which is a counterexample?
options: A car turning at constant speed.
A puck gliding straight at constant velocity with balanced forces.
cpa.guide: Zero net force constrains change in velocity, not the velocity value.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
